items.stem: Economic development is best described as
options: an improvement in living standards, including health, education, freedom and reduced poverty
a rise in the money supply
an increase in real GDP only
items.answer: an improvement in living standards, including health, education, freedom and reduced poverty
items.markingKey: Broader than growth in real GDP.

items.stem: Explain why economic growth is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for economic development.
items.answer: Growth provides resources to improve health, education and infrastructure, but whether development occurs depends on how income is distributed and used, and on environmental and social impacts.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: growth provides resources; 1 mark: distribution/use determines development [2]

items.stem: Explain two ways in which economic development can promote further economic growth.
items.answer: Better health and education raise labour productivity; reduced poverty increases saving and demand; better institutions attract investment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each identified, 1 mark each explained [4]

items.stem: Real GDP in Dravonia grows by 4% and population by 1.5%. Calculate the growth of real GDP per head.

In Gorvania, nominal GDP grew by 9% last year, the GDP deflator rose by 5% and the population grew by 1%. Life expectancy and school enrolment were unchanged, while the share of income going to the top 10% rose. Calculate the growth in real GDP and real GDP per head, and explain whether the country has experienced economic development.
items.answer: Real GDP ≈ 3.81%; real GDP per head ≈ 2.78%. Growth has occurred, but with unchanged health and education and rising inequality, there is little evidence of development.
items.markingKey: Deflate nominal growth [1]; adjust for population [1]; distinguish growth from development using the indicators [2].

items.stem: Extract: Real GDP in Gorvania has grown by 7% a year for a decade, mainly from oil exports. Population grows at 2.5% a year. Life expectancy has risen only from 61 to 62 years and many rural households lack electricity. (a) Calculate the approximate annual growth of real GDP per head. (b) Explain why the HDI may be a better indicator of development than GDP per head here.
items.answer: (a) 4.5% (exactly 4.39%) (b) Includes health and education; would show limited progress.

items.stem: Sundara’s GDP has risen rapidly due to mining, but most profits go to foreign owners and mining areas suffer pollution. Explain why this may not be economic development.
items.answer: Development requires improvements in living standards for most people; if gains flow abroad or to a few, and health and environment worsen, welfare may not improve.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: definition; 1 mark: application [2]

items.stem: Explain two advantages of the HDI over GDP per head as a measure of living standards.
items.answer: It includes health and education, not just income; it uses PPP-adjusted income; the income index uses logs, reflecting diminishing returns to income.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each identified, 1 mark each explained [4]

items.stem: Real GDP in Esteria grows by 4% and population by 2.5%. Calculate the growth of real GDP per head.
Real GDP in Rovania grows by 3% and population by 3%. Calculate the growth of real GDP per head.

In Quentara, nominal GDP grew by 8% last year, the GDP deflator rose by 3% and the population grew by 1%. Life expectancy and school enrolment were unchanged, while the share of income going to the top 10% rose. Calculate the growth in real GDP and real GDP per head, and explain whether the country has experienced economic development.
items.answer: Real GDP ≈ 4.85%; real GDP per head ≈ 3.82%. Growth has occurred, but with unchanged health and education and rising inequality, there is little evidence of development.
items.markingKey: Deflate nominal growth [1]; adjust for population [1]; distinguish growth from development using the indicators [2].

items.stem: The Human Development Index combines measures of
options: health (life expectancy), education (years of schooling) and income (GNI per head at PPP)
items.answer: health (life expectancy), education (years of schooling) and income (GNI per head at PPP)
items.markingKey: Geometric mean of three dimension indices.

items.stem: Explain two limitations of the HDI.
items.answer: Ignores inequality within the country, environmental damage, political freedom and the informal economy; equal weights are arbitrary; data quality.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each identified, 1 mark each explained [4]

items.stem: Explain how the MPI differs from income-based measures of poverty.
items.answer: It measures deprivations directly in health, education and living standards (e.g. nutrition, schooling, sanitation, electricity), so it captures aspects of poverty that income does not.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: dimensions; 1 mark: contrast with income measure [2]

items.stem: Life expectancy in Korvia is 71.5 years. Using the HDI formula (LE − 20)/(85 − 20), calculate the life expectancy index.

Data for Sundara: life expectancy 67 years; mean years of schooling 7.5; expected years of schooling 16; GNI per head (PPP) $1,500. Using the UNDP method (LEI = (LE − 20)/65; EI = (MYS/15 + EYS/18)/2; II = (ln GNI − ln 100)/(ln 75,000 − ln 100); HDI = geometric mean), calculate the HDI and identify which dimension most limits it.
items.answer: LEI = 0.723; EI = 0.694; II = 0.409; HDI = 0.59. The lowest index (income) limits it most.
items.markingKey: Each dimension index [3]; geometric mean (LEI × EI × II)^(1/3) [1]; identification [1].

items.stem: Data for Esteria: life expectancy 80.5 years; mean years of schooling 4.5; expected years of schooling 12.5; GNI per head (PPP) $25,000. Using the UNDP method (LEI = (LE − 20)/65; EI = (MYS/15 + EYS/18)/2; II = (ln GNI − ln 100)/(ln 75,000 − ln 100); HDI = geometric mean), calculate the HDI and identify which dimension most limits it.
items.answer: LEI = 0.931; EI = 0.497; II = 0.834; HDI = 0.728. The lowest index (education) limits it most.
items.markingKey: Each dimension index [3]; geometric mean (LEI × EI × II)^(1/3) [1]; identification [1].

Life expectancy has risen only from 61 to 62 years and many rural households lack electricity. (a) Calculate the approximate annual growth of real GDP per head. (b) Explain why the HDI may be a better indicator of development than GDP per head here.
items.answer: (a) 3.5% (exactly 3.41%) (b) Includes health and education; would show limited progress.

items.stem: Extract: Real GDP in Gorvania has grown by 6% a year for a decade, mainly from oil exports. Population grows at 2.5% a year. Life expectancy has risen only from 61 to 62 years and many rural households lack electricity. (a) Explain why the data suggest growth without much development. (b) Explain why the HDI may be a better indicator of development than GDP per head here.
items.answer: (a) Health barely improved; deprivation persists; oil revenue may be concentrated; inequality. (b) Includes health and education; would show limited progress.

items.stem: The Measure of Economic Welfare (MEW) adjusts GDP by
options: adding the value of leisure and non-market activity and subtracting “bads” such as pollution
items.answer: adding the value of leisure and non-market activity and subtracting “bads” such as pollution
items.markingKey: Nordhaus–Tobin.

items.stem: Valdoria and Gorvania have similar GNI per head, but Valdoria has a much higher HDI. Explain how this could happen.
items.answer: Valdoria may spend more on public health and education, or distribute income more equally, so life expectancy and schooling are higher for the same income.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: health/education; 1 mark: policy/distribution [2]

items.stem: Life expectancy in Umbria Nova is 58 years. Using the HDI formula (LE − 20)/(85 − 20), calculate the life expectancy index.

In Kestria, 40% of the population are multidimensionally poor and, on average, they are deprived in 55% of the weighted indicators. Calculate the MPI and explain what it shows that an income poverty line would not.
items.answer: MPI = 0.40 × 0.55 = 0.22. It shows both how many are poor and how intensely, across health, education and living standards, not just income.
items.markingKey: MPI = H × A [2]; interpretation [1].

items.stem: Data for Korvia: life expectancy 80.5 years; mean years of schooling 11; expected years of schooling 11; GNI per head (PPP) $3,000. Using the UNDP method (LEI = (LE − 20)/65; EI = (MYS/15 + EYS/18)/2; II = (ln GNI − ln 100)/(ln 75,000 − ln 100); HDI = geometric mean), calculate the HDI and identify which dimension most limits it.
items.answer: LEI = 0.931; EI = 0.672; II = 0.514; HDI = 0.685. The lowest index (income) limits it most.
items.markingKey: Each dimension index [3]; geometric mean (LEI × EI × II)^(1/3) [1]; identification [1].

items.stem: Valdoria ranks 60 places higher on GNI per head than on the HDI. (a) Explain how the HDI is calculated. (b) Assess whether the Human Development Index is the best indicator of living standards.
items.answer: (a) Explanation of the theory (with a described diagram where relevant), drawing on: Broader than GDP, includes health and education. (b) Case for the view: Broader than GDP, includes health and education. Case against / evaluation: Ignores inequality, environment, freedom; MPI and MEW capture other aspects; data quality. Conclusion: a judgement on the conditions under which the view holds.

(b) Analysis of arguments for and against; evaluation reaches a justified conclusion that weighs the conditions under which the claim holds. Top level needs a judgement, not just a summary.

items.stem: To compare living standards between countries, GDP per head should be converted using
items.answer: purchasing power parity exchange rates
items.markingKey: Adjusts for differences in price levels.

items.stem: To compare living standards over time within a country, economists use
items.answer: real GDP per head
items.markingKey: Removes the effect of inflation and population change.

items.stem: Explain two problems in using real GDP per head to compare living standards over time.
items.answer: Changes in quality and new products; changes in distribution; changes in hours worked and leisure; environmental costs; growth of the informal economy or non-market activity.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each identified, 1 mark each explained [4]

items.stem: Korvia has GDP of $800 billion and a population of 40 million. Calculate GDP per head.
items.markingKey: 800 billion/40 million = $20,000.

items.stem: A report compares living standards in Sundara, Loristan and Korvia. ‘GDP per head is an unreliable way to compare living standards between countries.’ Evaluate this statement.
items.answer: Arguments for: Price levels, informal economy, distribution and non-market output differ. Arguments against / evaluation: PPP adjustment helps; GDP still correlates with health and education; combine with other indicators. Conclusion: a supported judgement that depends on the conditions identified.
items.markingKey: Knowledge and analysis (about 60%): accurate theory, logical chains of reasoning and a relevant diagram described with axes, curves and shifts. Evaluation (about 40%): considers both sides, the assumptions and the context, and reaches a justified conclusion.

items.answer: People have less leisure, which has value; stress and health may suffer; the gain per hour worked is lower; GDP excludes leisure.
